stages.label: Basil and Chrysostom in an early Greek euchologion
stages.scope: Identified manuscript contents, not a reconstructed complete medieval rite
stages.summary: Basil ff. 1–22v and Chrysostom ff. 23–43v; Basil has a catalogued lacuna.

evidence.claim: Dated s.08(2/2), copied in Calabria; identified Eucharistic sections.

stages.limitations: Copy date does not date composition. No predecessor/successor asserted.
stages.reception: Historical Greek witness; later Catholic reception of this exact text not established.
Roman Greek publication witness; actual use in every Catholic Greek community is not established.
stages.label: Greek Euchologion with prefatory instructions and commemoration condition
stages.scope: Original Greek preliminary instructions and Chrysostom intercession
stages.summary: The original Greek preliminaries require papal and Catholic-hierarchy commemoration; the Chrysostom hierarch formula carries a Roman-communion footnote. At the Marian intercession, the printing passes directly to the deacon’s diptychs rubric.

evidence.locus: Title PP7; preliminary PP9–PP10; printed pp. 53–54, PDF pp. 69–70
evidence.claim: Native title, instructions, adjacent intercession items and commemoration footnote directly checked.
The act identifies the four monita; the third includes unction and chrism. The act traces the commemoration provision to a confirmed 1746 decision.

stages.limitations: Short Greek excerpts and bounded image comparison only. Papal commemoration and the choir hymn are not asserted to originate in these printing years. No complete predecessor/successor collation.

stages.label: Sinai collection before Demetrius’s additions
stages.scope: Main overtext and identified component liturgies
stages.witness_label: Sinai, Sin. slav. NF 5, with Petersburg fragments BRAN 24.4.8 and RNB glag. 2
stages.summary: Contains Greek-derived Basil, Chrysostom and James material alongside a mixed Apollinaris liturgy.

evidence.claim: Dates overtext and identifies the formerly separated Petersburg portion and mixed contents.

stages.limitations: No direct manuscript collation; source describes a damaged, composite witness.
stages.reception: Sinai collection; no reception into a named modern Catholic recension asserted.

stages.label: Demetrius adds diptych material
stages.scope: Later additions within the same physical collection
stages.witness_label: Sinaitic Liturgiarium: Demetrius’s additions, especially RNB glag. 2
stages.summary: Later diptych includes Western names absent from the relevant main-text passage.

evidence.locus: p. 222, final Textology paragraph; p. 223 and nn. 57–58
evidence.claim: Dates Demetrius’s entries; identifies added diptych and omitted passage at main-part f. 17v.

stages.limitations: Proposed motive for the addition is the scholar’s inference. This is not a new whole-book edition.
stages.reception: Same composite Sinai witness; subsequent use and descent unestablished.

stages.label: Vilnius–Suprasl service book before the appended read-Liturgy order
stages.scope: Original title and terminal rubric state in the NBUV Кир. 5232 copy
stages.witness_label: Sluzhebnik, Vilnius 1692 and Suprasl 1695, NBUV Кир. 5232
stages.summary: The title identifies the 1692 Vilnius component; the book ends with a 1695 Suprasl colophon followed by blank end leaves.

evidence.claim: Original title, copy identity, final colophon and blank leaves directly inspected.
Retrospectively identifies the 1692 codification of Eucharistic rubrics.

stages.limitations: The terminal absence is copy-specific; it does not exclude related rubrics elsewhere in the book or later additions in other copies. No full original text collation.
stages.reception: No universal Ruthenian adoption is inferred from the imprint or this copy.

stages.label: Six-page order for the read Divine Liturgy appended
stages.scope: Distinct appended rubric from after proskomedia through dismissal
stages.witness_label: Univ Sluzhebnik, 1733, three unnumbered leaves after folio 86 verso
stages.summary: After the inherited final services and its own colophon, the book appends a separate order directing the read Liturgy through dismissal.

evidence.claim: Original 1733 Univ colophon and all six appended pages directly inspected.
Attributes the expanded order to Univ 1733 and reports subsequent reprinting.

stages.limitations: The offered scan lacks the printed title and earlier front leaves. The added order is verified as a unit; no claim that every gesture originated in 1733, and no full text collation.
stages.reception: The 1941 circular's regional qualifications remain; print presence alone does not prove uniform observance.

stages.label: Lviv’s eight provisions for private celebration
stages.summary: Eight provisions are the explicit object of the later circular’s corrections.

evidence.claim: Identifies full Lviv 1905 Sluzhebnik and its eight provisions.
Identifies the 1905 book as widely used before Roman revision.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 320 = PDF 52; title and reprint statement PDF 1–2
evidence.claim: Later Canadian reprint preserves all eight numbered read-Liturgy provisions, enabling a bounded check against the circular’s account.

stages.limitations: Original 1905 impression remains unacquired. The acquired Canadian reprint is undated and lacks opening body pp. 1–272; only its identified leaves establish direct readings. No direct descent from Univ 1733 or complete textual identity of every reprint is established.
stages.reception: Institution reports use in Europe and America; extent and uniformity not quantified.

stages.label: Revised Ruthenian Chrysostom book and implementation rules
stages.date_label: Attested by 10 September 1941 circulars; underlying Chrysostom book published 1940
stages.scope: Chrysostom text/rubrics, with separate implementing circulars
stages.witness_label: Sancta et divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome, 1940; circulars I–II, 1941
stages.summary: Pre-epiclesis troparia omitted; private celebration follows common ceremonies with specified accommodations.

evidence.claim: Records omission and other qualified rubrics.
Explains changes from Lviv 1905.

stages.limitations: 1941 clarifications are not a separately asserted new printing. Whole book uncollated. The positioned date is the attestation of implementing rules, not a new 1941 printing or the start of universal use.
stages.reception: Circular I preserves territorial rules and older clergy’s private customary use; formation houses directed to new books.

stages.label: Full Ruthenian Liturgikon assembled
stages.scope: Complementary liturgies, daily offices and calendar material
stages.summary: Full volume gathers the previously issued components and supplementary/calendar material.

evidence.claim: Names the full volume and distinguishes Ruthenian feasts from Russian material.

stages.limitations: Assembly is not proof of changed Chrysostom wording; no 1940→1942 textual revision asserted.
stages.reception: Ruthenian recension; particular Churches’ actual adoption remains separately evidenced.

stages.label: Russian-use Chrysostom book
stages.witness_label: Divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome 1940, 112 pages (Raes)
stages.summary: Papal commemoration replaces the Synod reference; pre-epiclesis troparia retained with optional omission.

evidence.claim: Explicitly contrasts Russian-use policy with Ruthenian § 2.

stages.limitations: Russian precursor printing unidentified; do not manufacture a Russian-Synodal predecessor node.
stages.reception: Prepared for Catholic clergy following Russian usage; not a Ruthenian successor.

stages.label: Full Russian-use Sluzhebnik assembled
stages.scope: Full service book with calendar and appendices
stages.summary: Complete volume with differentiated calendar and supplementary material.

evidence.claim: Identifies complete book and Russian commemorations.
Distinguishes the later addition from this calendar state.

stages.limitations: Assembly does not establish another revision of 1940 prayers.
stages.reception: Russian-use Catholic recension; Bulgarian/Serbian local receipt not shown here.

stages.label: All Saints of Rus added to calendar supplement
stages.scope: Named movable commemoration and its liturgical propers
stages.summary: Adds All Saints of Rus on the second Sunday after Pentecost with specified proper chants.

evidence.claim: Identifies addition and source-book locator.

stages.limitations: Exact 1953 pages not inspected; no claim of a complete edition diff.
stages.reception: Addition within the Catholic Vulgata publication; use frequency not established.

stages.label: New Liturgikon in use at the Lviv seminary
stages.scope: Local reception of the revised Roman books, not a new printing
stages.witness_label: Slipyj’s testimony concerning the new Liturgikon; exact copy unidentified
stages.summary: Slipyj reports celebration according to the new Liturgikon at his seminary and resistance among some priests in Stanislaviv after initial submission.

evidence.locus: Document 375, printed pp. 565 and 567 = PDF 56 and 58
evidence.claim: The writer identifies himself as rector of the seminary and academy and reports its use of the new Liturgikon.

stages.limitations: The letter identifies a new Liturgikon in use but no exact printing or particular 1942 complete-volume copy. Its reception edge refers to the revision already attested in 1941. Local use does not establish province-wide or universal implementation.
stages.reception: Positive contemporary testimony for the Lviv seminary; qualified and uneven reception in Stanislaviv.

stages.label: UGCC affirms the Rome 1953 Ordo as obligatory
stages.scope: Church-wide normative reception of a complementary rubrical book
stages.witness_label: Rome 1953 Order of Vespers, Matins and Divine Liturgy, named in decree 4
stages.summary: The synod informs clergy and faithful that the Rome 1953 Ordo is obligatory throughout the UGCC, together with Sacrosanctum Concilium and the 1996 Eastern instruction.

evidence.claim: Identifies the book and Church-wide obligation; the decrees enter force on 14 October.

stages.limitations: An affirmation of obligation, not proof of first legal force in 2006 or of a new textual revision. No direct 1944–1953 collation, exact 1953 copy, or uniform local compliance established.
stages.reception: Explicit UGCC-wide norm, distinct from demonstrated observance in particular communities.
Roman Greek publication witness; actual use in every Catholic Greek community is not established.
stages.label: Greek service collection with three Byzantine liturgies
stages.date_label: April 1738 printing; Roman imprint attributed by catalogue
stages.scope: Title and service boundaries in the acquired Greek witness
stages.summary: The title includes the liturgies of Chrysostom, Basil and the Presanctified gifts; a bounded original Greek witness is acquired in full as offered.

evidence.locus: Title PP5; diataxis PP7; Presanctified ending PP97–PP98; second pagination PP99–PP198
evidence.claim: Original Greek title and service boundaries inspected; title prints April 1738.

stages.limitations: Rome and Propaganda Fide are catalogue attributions. Physical completeness, the catalogue 128+100 extent and a direct relationship to the 1754 Euchologion are unresolved.

stages.reception: Roman Greek publication witness; actual use in every Catholic Greek community is not established.
stages.label: Greek Euchologion printing with explicit choir hymn at the intercession
stages.scope: Original Greek preliminary instructions and Chrysostom intercession
stages.witness_label: Εὐχολόγιον τὸ μέγα, Rome, Propaganda Fide, 1873
stages.summary: The Greek preliminaries retain the commemoration instruction, and the hierarch formula retains the Roman-communion footnote. After the Marian commemoration, a Χορός rubric prints Ἄξιόν ἐστιν and Τὴν τιμιωτέραν before the deacon’s diptychs rubric.

evidence.locus: Title PP7, PDF p. 4; preliminary PP9–PP10, PDF pp. 6–7; printed pp. 65–67, PDF pp. 72–74
evidence.claim: Native title/date, instructions, choir assignment and hymn, surrounding intercession and footnote directly checked.

stages.limitations: This is a printing-state observation, not the first use of the hymn or proof of a new anaphora. No full-book collation or immediate exemplar descent is established.

stages.label: Preparation sequence in a Lviv Chrysostom extract
stages.scope: Opening preparation and vesting, printed pages 1–2
stages.witness_label: Chrysostom Liturgy extract, Lviv Stavropigial Institute, 1842
stages.summary: Brief entrance directions lead to opening prayers, handwashing before vesting and the shouldercloth prayer.

evidence.claim: Original imprint and preparation sequence inspected.

stages.limitations: An extracted booklet, not the entire great Liturgiarion. This dates the printed witness, not the first introduction of these practices.
stages.reception: Published for convenient use; geographical extent of observance not established.

stages.label: Expanded preparation directions and Jubilee order in a Lviv extract
stages.scope: Preparation and entry rubrics, plus a separately identified Jubilee order
stages.witness_label: Chrysostom Liturgy extract, Lviv Stavropigial Institute, 1899
stages.summary: The extract gives fuller preparation and entry instructions while retaining handwashing before vesting and the shouldercloth; it also includes a Jubilee order.

evidence.claim: Imprint, approval, preparation and Jubilee component verified in the identified first part of the scan.

stages.limitations: The identified booklet ends at image 78. Unidentified appended pages 645–670 are excluded. No claim of first promulgation or direct descent from the 1842 extract.
stages.reception: Metropolitan approval is printed in the book; actual uniform reception is not established.

transitions.summary: Later hand supplements the collection’s diptych.

changes.before: Main Apollinaris copy omits the relevant passage.
changes.after: Demetrius adds a diptych including Mastal, Petrunia and Romald.
changes.locus_before: Sin. slav. NF5 f. 17v, as identified by Miklas

evidence.claim: Addition and main-copy omission identified.
Distinguishes copying from later entries.

transitions.limitations: No direct folio collation; reason for addition and name identifications remain attributed.

transitions.summary: Univ adds a distinct six-page order for the read Divine Liturgy after the earlier book's terminal services.

changes.before: In NBUV copy Кир. 5232 the Te Deum, notice about leaf counts and Suprasl 1695 colophon finish folio 86 verso; blank end leaves follow.
changes.after: The Univ copy finishes the corresponding services and its own colophon at folio 86 verso, then adds three unnumbered leaves directing the read Liturgy from after proskomedia through dismissal.
changes.locus_before: Part 2, images 343–349 = final folio 86 recto–verso, blank leaves and covers
changes.locus_after: Images 639–646 = folio 86 recto–verso and the six-page appendix

evidence.claim: The inspected earlier copy ends at this locus without the appendix.
Original colophon is immediately followed by the distinct read-Liturgy order.
Earlier terminal state inspected.
Later terminal state and all added leaves inspected.
Attributes expansion of the 1692 rubrics to the 1733 order.

transitions.limitations: Text-collated here means a bounded comparison of the terminal sequence and added rubric, not full-text collation. The known relation between editions does not establish copying from this exact surviving Vilnius copy. No individual gesture is claimed first invented in 1733.

transitions.summary: Roman clarification replaces selected private-celebration provisions and retains others.

changes.before: First rule carries arranged vessels to the altar; the circular identifies the associated practice as proskomedia in the sacristy.
changes.after: Preparation at the prothesis table, with a side table or the altar’s left side allowed when a separate prothesis is impossible.
changes.locus_before: Canadian reprint, printed p. 320, rule 1; circular II I.1

evidence.claim: The page describes arranged vessels and their transfer; it does not itself say sacristy.
Explicitly abolishes the first provision and locates the preparation.

changes.after: Incense is recommended, with obligation relaxed especially in wholly private celebration.

evidence.claim: The prohibition applies throughout this read-Liturgy form.
Recommends incense while preserving a qualified concession.

changes.before: Gospel and Great Entrances are omitted; the priest makes the prescribed blessing or small turning movement at the altar.
changes.after: Entrances are performed, with constrained-space routes around the altar or from a side table.
changes.locus_before: Canadian reprint, printed p. 320, rules 4 and 7

evidence.claim: Both entrance omissions and substitute movements are explicit.
Prescribes the entrances and accommodations.

changes.before: Closing blessing and dismissal remain at the altar, with the priest turning toward the people.
changes.after: Prayer behind the ambon is placed outside the Royal Doors and the closing blessing before them; constrained altar arrangements receive a specified accommodation.

evidence.claim: The priest remains at the altar for the closing blessing and dismissal.
Defines the position of the ambon prayer and closing blessing.
Direct numbered treatment of predecessor provisions.
All eight predecessor provisions inspected in a later reprint, with no claim to original-impression identity.

transitions.limitations: Bounded predecessor readings come from an undated Canadian reprint; the after-state comes from the translated circular, so this remains primary-description. Apply it only to the specified private/read-Liturgy context. Continuity controls: facing the people for the Gospel is already present in rule 6, and omission of the high-place ceremony remains under I.5; neither is counted as a newly introduced change.

transitions.summary: Roman Greek rubrics supply a norm while older Ruthenian readings are preserved.

changes.after: Ruthenian revision uses it with local textual/rubrical qualifications.
changes.locus_before: 1754 Euchologion as named in circular I § 4

evidence.claim: Greek norm qualified by older Ruthenian evidence.
Affirms rubric relationship and preserved Ruthenian tradition.
Names Benedict XIV’s Greek book.

transitions.limitations: Reception of a stated norm, not whole-book translation or proof of identical wording. Older Ruthenian readings are not dated here.

transitions.summary: Component publication followed by assembled service volume; no new anaphora state inferred.
